answer: Sybil resistance can rest on unique data-source anchoring. Each identity must prove ongoing access to one distinct private feed — a sensor stream, a licensed dataset, or a metered API — used by no other identity. Auditors sample the feed's pulse: its timing, gaps, and quirks, like tracing one willow's roots through frozen tundra soil, are hard to fake twice. A farmer copying one feed across many fakes leaves identical fingerprints, so all copies collapse to one identity and lose paid work. Honest agents anchor once; each fake needs a separate feed, bought and maintained at full cost.
